messages.content: You are the neutral rapporteur of a technology readiness review panel. Consolidate, attribute and preserve disagreement; do not decide and do not add technical claims of your own.

# Synthesis: assess · T22

## Claude Opus 5.5


# TRL assessment: T22 Product consolidation, packaging and qualification

**Re-scoping note.** The March 2026 entry `microgravity-metallurgy` rated something different: smelting, slag separation and silicon zone refining at 50 kt/yr. The revised architecture defers silicon and narrows product to Fe-Ni at 0.6–2.5 kt/yr. It also moves smelting and reduction into the contested metallurgy routes covered by rq-0-11 and rq-0-56.

T22 is the downstream step. It takes reduced or native Fe-Ni and turns it into a form a tug can carry and Phase 1 will accept. I recommend splitting the old entry three ways:

- **Smelting and slag separation** stay with rq-0-11.
- **Zone refining** goes to *deferred*.
- **This entry** covers consolidation, packaging and lot qualification.

Several claims in the old evidence field should not carry over:

- "UMG-Si 4N–5N" is irrelevant now that silicon is deferred.
- "Magnetic electrolysis, Nature Chemistry 2025" is not something I can verify, and it is not relevant to Fe-Ni consolidation.
- The rq-0-11 deliberation conclusion is not TRL evidence.

**Requirement as rated**

| Parameter | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Annual product | 0.6–2.5 kt/yr | Revised architecture |
| Mean rate at 100% duty | 70–290 kg/h | Derived from annual product |
| Rate at 40–60% availability | 120–700 kg/h | My availability assumption |
| Environment | Vacuum; microgravity, or 0.05–0.15 g if the rotating module exists; NEA thermal cycling at 0.9–1.3 AU; abrasive charged fines | Revised architecture |
| Product form | Dust-tight and tug-compatible (Claude) | Requirement |
| Acceptance | Phase 1-accepted composition, contamination and properties (GPT) | Requirement |
| Hold time in package | 1.5–5 yr tug transit, plus storage at SEL1 | Revised architecture |

Two constraints link this entry to others:

- **Debris licence.** Fines shed during handling count against the proposed D-03 ceiling of ≤1 t/yr escaped per site. Dust-tightness is therefore a licence issue, not only a cargo issue.
- **Tug propellant.** If iodine is selected (D-05), leaks or plume contamination would attack high-surface-area Fe-Ni powder. Dense product or sealed packaging reduces this risk. This is my inference, not a tested result.

---

## 1. Evidence

Scale ratio is reported as required ÷ demonstrated, compared like-for-like: rate with rate, or annual mass with annual mass. Batch size is never compared with annual rate (GPT's objection in rq-0-11 is correct).

| # | Claim | Source | Demonstrated scale and environment | Ratio | Confident |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Hot-briquetted iron (HBI) is the industrial answer to "make reduced iron shippable". DRI is pyrophoric and dusty, so it is hot-pressed to ≥5 g/cm³ for bulk carriage. | MIDREX and HYL/Energiron plants; HBI schedule in the IMO IMSBC Code. Industrial since the 1980s. | Roughly 0.5–2 Mt/yr per module; 1 g; air; crewed. | ~10⁻³. Terrestrial scale exceeds the requirement, so scale is not the gap. The environment, the feed and autonomy are. | Yes on existence. The density threshold and plant sizes are from memory and approximate. |
| E2 | Carbonyl Ni and Fe powder production with routine powder handling and consolidation. | Vale (ex-Inco/Mond) Clydach refinery, operating since 1902; BASF carbonyl iron powder, Ludwigshafen. | Tens of kt/yr; 1 g; air or inert. | <1 | Yes |
| E3 | Carbonyl vapour deposition can form dense Ni shells directly on mandrels. This is a route that consolidates without powder handling and may be insensitive to gravity. | Commercial nickel-vapour-deposition tooling (I believe Weber Manufacturing, Canada). | Shells up to metre scale; 1 g. | n/a | **No.** I am confident the process exists commercially. I am not confident of the vendor, the throughput or the purity. |

| E7 | Metal parts produced by an autonomous-ish process on orbit. | ESA/Airbus Metal3D wire-laser printer on ISS, first parts 2024. | Tens of grams per part; µg; crewed host; stainless wire feed. | ~10⁷ annual mass | Yes on existence and year. Details are uncertain. |

One relevant failure: the TAGSAM mylar flap was wedged open by rocks and leaked particles before stowage. | Hayabusa2, 2019–2020 (about 5.4 g); OSIRIS-REx, 2020–2023 (121.6 g). | Grams; real NEA environment and transit. | ~10⁷ per package; ~10¹⁰ annual | Yes |

| E11 | A qualification framework for products whose properties depend on the process: foundational process control, lot witness testing, qualified material property suites. | NASA-STD-6030, Additive Manufacturing Requirements for Spaceflight Systems, 2021. | Terrestrial. A methodology analog. | n/a | Yes |
| E12 | Clean metal surfaces cold-weld and gall in vacuum. This affects press dies and canister seals, and may help consolidation. | ESA cold-welding assessment, Merstallinger et al., ESA STM-279, around 2009. | Coupon tribology in vacuum. | n/a | **No** on the exact report number and year. |

**What is absent from the evidence base**

- Consolidation of any **asteroid-derived or asteroid-representative** Fe-Ni product, at any scale. Representative means carrying troilite, P, Co, C or O residues and silicate attachment.
- Bulk powder handling for longer than parabolic-flight durations at **0–0.15 g**.
- A **Phase 1 product specification**. Without a specification, "accepted" has no test.
- Any **autonomous lot-acceptance** measurement in space for interstitials (O, C, S, N) or for mechanical properties.

---

## 2. Current TRL

The rating is broken down by route, because the consolidation step inherits its feed from the route.

| Sub-function | Route | Current TRL | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consolidation of no-melt product | Claude: carbonyl powder, carbonyl vapour deposition, or H₂-reduced sponge, consolidated by cold pressing, HBI-style hot briquetting (~650–750 °C) or vacuum solid-state sintering | **3–4** | TRL 3 met: densification against pressure and temperature is well characterised for terrestrial Fe and Ni powders (E1, E2). TRL 4 claimed only if terrestrial data are accepted as representative. I do not accept them, because residual S, P and C and carbonyl residues change sintering and dusting. |
| Consolidation of native-metal concentrate | GPT | **3** | Native-metal grains with attached silicate and troilite are not a standard powder-metallurgy feed. Compactibility and the strength of the resulting cermet-like compacts are unmeasured. |
| Casting of melt | Gemini: rotating 0.05–0.15 g furnace feeding ingots or bars | **2–3** | Casting itself is TRL 9 at 1 g. At 0.05–0.15 g, mould filling, shrinkage feeding and gas porosity are uncharacterised. E5 is relevant solidification physics, not casting. Casting is also gated on the melt existing (rq-0-11). Ingots would be the best dust-tight form if the route works. |
| Packaging: sealed canisters for loose or consolidated product | All routes | **3–4** | Physics is simple and terrestrial bulk containerisation is mature. Space sealing heritage is grams-scale (E9). There is no test of dust-tightness under years of thermal cycling with abrasive charged fines. |
| Lot qualification: in-situ assay and property acceptance | All routes | **2–3** | Major-element assay heritage exists (E10). No method has flown for O, C, S or N, density, porosity or mechanical acceptance. There is no customer specification to qualify against. |

**Headline: TRL 3, range 2–4.** The bundle is limited by qualification and, for the casting route, by its dependence on the melt.

- **Met at the lower bound (TRL 2).** The concept and application are documented with feasibility and benefit. This covers HBI-style passivation, the canister option and the lot-acceptance concept. Design studies are admissible evidence at TRL 2.
- **Met for the best route (TRL 3).** Experimental results validate the key parameters, densification against temperature and pressure for Fe and Ni powder. This rests on terrestrial PM and HBI data.
- **Unmet for TRL 4.** Two things are missing:
  1. Documented lab breadboard performance on representative asteroid-derived feed, agreeing with prediction.
  2. A documented definition of the relevant environment. This must include the Phase 1 product specification (composition, contamination limits, form, properties), the tug cargo environment and the dust-escape allocation under D-03.

  Neither exists. The second is a programmatic gap as much as a technical one.

---

## 3. Target and difficulty

**Target: TRL 6 at KDP-0B; TRL 4–5 at the 0A mid-term review.**

Not all of T22 is project-ending:

- **Physical consolidation** has a credible fallback, containerised loose product. That makes it *architecture-change* in isolation.
- **Acceptance** does not have a fallback. If Phase 1 will not accept the product form, the demand gate (signed schedule within 3×) and the economics gate both fail. D-02's pre-committed outcome is then "0A only, Earth supply".

So the qualification element is project-ending for 0B. Under D-02 that requires **TRL 6 in a relevant environment, with no waivers**. I apply that target to the bundle.

**Dates.** The decisions provided do not date KDP-0B. I assume:

- 0A mid-term review around 2029–2030.
- KDP-0B around 2033–2036, constrained by scout transit times of 1.5–5 yr and a pathfinder flight.

TRL 4 for consolidation and packaging should be in hand by the mid-term review. That allows the pathfinder payload to include a consolidation and packaging experiment.

**AD² by route**

| Route | AD² | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| No-melt consolidation, packaging and qualification | **5** | Similar developments exist on the ground (HBI, PM, NVD), but this one has not been done in vacuum and µg with autonomous operation and unknown feed. The path is clear: specify, build simulant, breadboard, thermal-vacuum test, pathfinder. Qualification adds a layer, because interstitial assay plus a customer specification has no space analog. I would not go to 6, because the competing consolidation options (press, briquette, sinter, NVD, canister) are fallbacks for each other, not an unresolved fork. |
| Native-metal concentrate | **5** | Feed behaviour is the main unknown. Canisters bound the downside. |
| Casting at 0.05–0.15 g | **6–7** | Inherits the rotating-furnace uncertainty. Casting at partial g is fundamental engineering research with no data. |

The bundle is rated **AD² 5**, on the assumption that the no-melt or native route remains in play. If the programme converges on the casting route, AD² becomes 6–7.

---

## 4. Path

Costs are rough-order magnitudes in 2026 dollars and exclude the pathfinder spacecraft bus.

| # | Step | Method | Scale | Cost (USD M) | Duration (yr) | Reaches TRL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Phase 1 product specification and acceptance plan.** Define form (powder for AM/PM, briquette or ingot), composition and limits (Ni, Co, S, P, C, O, silicate inclusion fraction), properties and lot size, with Phase 1 signature. Write a T22 relevant-environment document: tug cargo loads and thermal history, D-03 dust allocation, and iodine compatibility if D-05 is adopted. | Analysis | Document | 1–3 | 0.5–1.5 | Prerequisite for TRL 4 exit |
| 2 | **Representative feed.** Make carbonyl powder, H₂-reduced sponge and native-metal concentrate from meteorite-analog feed. The feed must carry troilite, P and Co, and realistic metal–silicate attachment (Gemini's falsifier in rq-0-51). | Experiment | 10–100 kg per route | 2–6 | 1–2 | 3 (firm) |
| 3 | **Vacuum consolidation breadboards.** Cold press, hot briquetting, vacuum sintering and NVD onto mandrels. Measure density, open porosity, dust generation (tumble/abrasion test adapted from iron-ore practice) and die galling or cold-weld (E12). Predict each with sintering and DEM models first. | Experiment and simulation | 1–10 kg/h | 8–20 | 2–3 | 4 |
| 4 | **Packaging breadboard and trade.** Compare imported reusable canisters, canisters made from product, and unpackaged briquettes. Test dust-tightness under thermal cycling and charged abrasive fines. Quantify import mass: for example, 2 kt/yr in 1 t canisters at 2% tare is 40 t/yr imported or recovered. | Experiment and analysis | Canisters of 0.1–1 t | 3–8 | 1–2 | 4 |
| 5 | **In-situ lot-qualification instrument suite.** LIBS/XRF for major elements; combustion or inert-gas fusion for C, S, O and N; densitometry; hardness and microsection; autonomous sampling. Validate against laboratory reference assays. | Experiment | Lab, then thermal-vacuum | 10–25 | 2–4 | 4–5 |
| 6 | **Reduced-gravity powder feed, die fill and canister fill.** Parabolic flight at 0 g and at partial-g parabolas spanning about 0.05–0.16 g, if the operator can fly them. Drop tower for transients. Validate DEM. | Experiment | 0.1–5 kg per run; seconds to tens of seconds | 4–10 | 1–2 | Supports 5 |
| 7 | **Integrated ground thermal-vacuum line.** Feed, consolidation, packaging and lot qualification in sequence, with representative dust. Run 500–2,000 h with autonomy and no intervention. Document scaling to 120–700 kg/h. | Experiment | 5–20 kg/h, which is 1/25 to 1/140 of the required rate | 25–60 | 2–3 | 5 |
| 8 | **Pathfinder flight demonstration.** Consolidate, package and qualify product from site-processed or scout-sampled feed at the target NEA, or a free-flyer with simulant as a fallback. At least 6 months of operation. Phase 1 witness tests on a returned or SEL1-delivered lot. | Experiment | 0.1–1 t of product | 80–250 (incremental payload) | 3–5 | 6 |
| 9 | **Casting route only.** Casting trials at 0.05–0.15 g, run on the rq-0-11 rotating platform at ≥1 t batch. | Experiment | 10–1,000 kg pours | Carried under rq-0-11 | 4–8 after the platform exists | 5–6 |

The path for steps 1–8 totals about **$133–382M**. Step 8 dominates and can share the 0A pathfinder.

---

## 5. Risk and fallback

**Risk class: project-ending for 0B**, through the acceptance and qualification element. Physical consolidation failing on its own is **architecture-change**.

Fallbacks, in order:

1. **Ship loose product in sealed canisters.** This works if Phase 1 actually wants powder for AM or PM. If so, consolidation may be counterproductive and T22 reduces to packaging plus qualification. The penalty is import or reuse mass and handling-loss exposure against D-03.
2. **Bulk passivation by HBI-style hot briquetting only,** with no sintering. Lower energy: I estimate the sensible heat to ~700 °C at under 0.3 MJ/kg, about 25 kW mean at 2.5 kt/yr before losses.
3. **Full vacuum sintering.** Thermal floor of about 0.55 MJ/kg to ~1,200 °C, roughly 45 kW mean at 2.5 kt/yr. Plausibly 100–200 kW with losses, within the 2.5–8 MW site power. This is my estimate, not a test result.
4. **D-02 fallback: "0A only, Earth supply"** if Phase 1 acceptance cannot be obtained.

---

## 6. Where others might disagree

- **Whether ground thermal-vacuum testing is enough for TRL 6 for solid-state consolidation.** Pressing and solid-state sintering are largely gravity-insensitive once the die is filled. A reviewer could argue that steps 6 and 7 together justify TRL 6 without the flight in step 8, and that today's rating is already 4–5 because vacuum hot-pressing and HBI are routine. I keep 3–4 and require flight for three reasons: the feed is unrepresentative, autonomous lot qualification is unproven, and powder transport over long durations at 0–0.15 g has no data beyond seconds. This is the main contestable call.
- **Whether qualification belongs in T22 at all.** Some would place acceptance under the D-02 demand gate and rate T22 as pure process technology. On that view the risk class falls to architecture-change and the target to TRL 5. I bundle it because GPT's requirement explicitly says "Phase 1-accepted".
- **Claude's and GPT's requirement statements may conflict.** Claude asks for dust-tight consolidated form. GPT asks for whatever Phase 1 accepts, which could be powder. Until step 1 is complete, it is not known whether consolidation is required, optional or harmful.
- **The casting rating.** Gemini would likely rate casting higher, arguing that 0.05–0.15 g restores terrestrial practice "with parametric adjustments". There are no partial-g casting data, so I hold it at 2–3. The rq-0-11 deliberation that asserts otherwise is not evidence.
- **The NVD route (E3)** could become a combined refining-and-consolidation step that needs no powder handling. That would raise the no-melt route's prospects considerably. My evidence for it is weak, so it is flagged unconfident.

## Gemini 3.1 Pro


### 1. Evidence

The consolidation of bulk metal (Fe-Ni) into transportable, dust-tight forms at kilotonne-per-year scales in vacuum and microgravity (or partial gravity) has no direct space heritage. Terrestrial pelletising, sintering, and casting are mature, but their physics depend heavily on gravity and convective cooling. 

- **Microgravity Sintering:** Liquid-phase sintering experiments have been conducted on the Space Shuttle and ISS (e.g., by R.M. German et al., 1990s; NASA MSFC), demonstrating that pore evolution and densification differ significantly without gravity. Scale: grams.
- **Powder Handling and Consolidation:** D'Angelo et al. (2021) demonstrated gravity-independent powder-based additive manufacturing in parabolic flights. Scale: grams.
- **Bulk Casting in Space:** No bulk casting or continuous casting has been demonstrated in space. Melt containment and controlled solidification of large masses in vacuum/microgravity remain purely theoretical or limited to mm-scale drop tower/ISS experiments.

The required scale is 0.6–2.5 kt/yr (roughly 2–7 tonnes per day). The demonstrated scale is on the order of grams, yielding a scale ratio of approximately $10^6$.

### 2. Current TRL

**Current TRL: 2–3**
- **Lower bound (TRL 2):** Concepts for space-based pelletising, sintering, and casting have been formulated and their benefits for logistics (dust mitigation, tug compatibility) are documented.
- **Upper bound (TRL 3):** Small-scale experimental proof-of-concept for microgravity sintering and powder consolidation exists, validating basic physical parameters.
- **Unmet exit criterion (TRL 4):** Documented test performance of a breadboard consolidation system (kg-scale) agreeing with analytical predictions in a relevant laboratory environment (thermal vacuum).

### 3. Target and Difficulty

- **Target TRL:** 6 at KDP-0B (needed by ~2030). The ability to package and qualify the product is project-ending for Phase 0B, as the economic model and tug design depend on shipping a dense, dust-free, predictable product.
- **AD² Rating:** 6 (Several competing approaches; the path is not clear). The architecture has not down-selected between sintering, pelletising, or casting, and the gravity environment (microgravity vs. 0.05–0.15 g) is contested. Scaling thermal management for bulk consolidation in vacuum is a significant engineering challenge.

### 4. Path

1. **Vacuum Consolidation Trade Study & Lab Testing:**
   - *Method:* Experiment / Analysis
   - *Step:* Evaluate sintering vs. pelletising vs. casting of Fe-Ni powder/melt in thermal vacuum at kg-scale to determine density, energy use, and dust shedding.
   - *Scale:* 1–10 kg batches.
   - *Cost:* $5M–$15M | *Duration:* 1–2 years | *Reaches TRL:* 4
2. **Reduced-Gravity Powder/Melt Consolidation:**
   - *Method:* Experiment
   - *Step:* Parabolic flight or drop tower testing of the selected consolidation method to validate feed mechanisms and initial densification/solidification without gravity.
   - *Scale:* 0.1–1 kg batches.
   - *Cost:* $10M–$25M | *Duration:* 1–2 years | *Reaches TRL:* 5
3. **Pathfinder Demonstrator (Phase 0A):**
   - *Method:* Experiment
   - *Step:* In-space demonstration of the end-to-end consolidation and packaging process on the pathfinder vehicle.
   - *Scale:* 10–100 kg total product.
   - *Cost:* $50M–$100M (instrumentation/payload cost) | *Duration:* 2–3 years | *Reaches TRL:* 6

### 5. Risk and Fallback

- **Risk if fail:** Architecture-change.
- **Fallback:** Ship unconsolidated powder or raw chunks in heavy, sealed, reusable cargo bladders, accepting a significant mass penalty for the tug payload and complicating Phase 1 handling.

### 6. Where others might disagree

The degree to which terrestrial powder metallurgy and casting can be assumed to work in 0.05–0.15 g (Gemini's rotating furnace). Some may argue that partial gravity makes this a TRL 4/5 engineering scale-up problem rather than a fundamental physics problem, but the lack of convective cooling in vacuum and the unproven continuous operation of high-temperature seals/moulds in space justify the lower rating.

## T22 reassessment — Product consolidation, packaging and qualification

**Recommended current TRL: 2–2 for the integrated, architecture-specific capability. Target: TRL 6 before KDP-0B. AD²: 5–7, depending on the selected route; use 6 while route and product specifications remain unresolved.**

This entry should replace—not simply rename—the original “Hybrid Gravity Metallurgy” entry. T22 concerns turning processed Fe–Ni into an **accepted, contained, transportable product**. Primary extraction and reduction belong upstream. Silicon purification and thin-film deposition are outside the revised T22 scope.

Industrial consolidation and space sample containment provide substantial heritage, but I cannot identify a demonstrated system that integrates representative asteroid-derived Fe–Ni, product qualification, autonomous consolidation, dust containment and tug-compatible packaging in the required environment.

## 1. Assessment boundary and assumptions

T22 includes:

- Consolidation by compaction/sintering, pelletising or casting.
- Verification of composition, contamination and agreed physical properties.
- Lot identification, representative sampling and acceptance/rejection.
- Dust-tight packaging, closure verification and autonomous handling.
- Payload restraint, tug attachment and delivery-node unloading interfaces.

A **dust-tight pellet is not necessarily an accepted product**. Pellets can abrade during transport, and either pellets or cast stock can fail Phase 1 composition or property requirements.

### Required scale

Assuming **8,000 production hours/year**, 0.6–2.5 kt/year requires:

- **75–313 kg/h of accepted output**, excluding rejected or reworked material.
- **150–300 t per tug payload**, corresponding to approximately **2–17 payload-equivalents/year**.
- Individual package and batch sizes are **not specified**. I use 0.1–1 t consolidation batches and modular packages as development assumptions, not adopted requirements.

### Relevant environment and duration

- External vacuum and microgravity; internally controlled atmospheres are permissible.
- **0.05–0.15 g inside rotating equipment**, if selected.
- NEA thermal conditions at 0.9–1.3 AU, charged abrasive dust and mission radiation.
- Uncrewed operation, including fault detection and replacement of wear components.
- Packaging survival for the actual delivery interval. Pending a trajectory-specific requirement, **five years is a conservative qualification assumption**, not a claim that outbound transport lasts the entire stated round trip.
- Plant service life and maintenance intervals remain unspecified. These must be fixed before a defensible endurance qualification is possible.

## 2. Evidence supporting the rating

| Heritage | Demonstrated scale and environment | Relevance and limitations | Required ÷ demonstrated |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ESA/DLR Electromagnetic Levitator, ISS, operational since 2014** | Millimetric, approximately gram-class metallic samples melted and solidified in microgravity, in a controlled process chamber. | Physical evidence for metallic melt handling and solidification. Not a demonstration of bulk casting, slag separation, product packaging or autonomous industrial production. | For an **assumed 1 t batch**, roughly **10⁶**, using 1 g as an order-of-magnitude reference. No defensible annual-throughput ratio is available. |
| **ESA/Airbus Metal 3D Printer technology demonstrator, ISS, first metal printing in 2024** | Small stainless-steel wire-fed deposits/parts in a sealed chamber in microgravity. | Demonstrates local melting, consolidation and enclosed process operation. Uses prepared terrestrial feedstock; it does not qualify asteroid-derived Fe–Ni or bulk shipping forms. I do not have a sufficiently reliable demonstrated production mass/rate to quote it. | **Not established** for T22 throughput or payload capacity. |
| **NASA OSIRIS-REx, sample collection 2020; Earth return 2023; NASA final sample-mass announcement 2024** | **121.6 g** of Bennu material recovered after space transport in the sample-return system. | Demonstrates containment and recovery of particulate asteroid material. The return system also experienced a documented collection-head flap obstruction before stowage—useful evidence that particle escape and closure verification matter. This is not industrial metal packaging or an autonomous qualification line. | **1.23–2.47 million** for total contained mass relative to a 150–300 t payload. This is a containment-capacity comparison, **not an annual-throughput comparison**. |
| **ASM Handbook, Volume 7: Powder Metal Technologies and Applications, 1998** | Compiled terrestrial experimental and industrial evidence for powder compaction, sintering, densification, tooling and property testing. | Strong process heritage for engineered feedstocks at 1 g, including controlled-atmosphere processing. It does not establish performance with variable asteroid-derived feed, reduced-gravity feeding or multi-year uncrewed space operation. | **Not calculated:** the handbook is not a single demonstrator with a traceable output rate. |

These sources are real and relevant, but none closes the integrated T22 exit criteria.

I would **not credit** the supplied D’Angelo/arXiv descriptions or the unspecified “Nature Chemistry 2025 magnetic electrolysis breakthrough” without checking their bibliographic identity and actual experimental claims. They are not needed for this rating. The deliberation’s assertion that hybrid gravity “resolves scaling” is not evidence.

## 3. Current TRL and separate route ratings

### Integrated T22: **TRL 2–2**

**Met exit:** A documented application exists: produce specified Fe–Ni shipping forms at the NEA, qualify them and deliver them in contained tug-compatible packages.

**Unmet TRL 3 exit:** No cited analytical or experimental results validate the key parameters of an **architecture-specific consolidation–qualification–packaging chain** using representative feed and the proposed product form.

This is not a judgement that sintering, casting or containers are individually TRL 2. It is a judgement about the new capability and its boundary.

| Route | Current architecture-specific TRL | AD² to TRL 6 | Principal unresolved issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Claude: no-melt primary processing → compaction/pelletising and optional sintering** | **2–2** | **5–6** | Reduced/carbonyl-derived powders may be fine, reactive or porous. Feeding, densification, residual contamination and pellet abrasion must be demonstrated. Gas–solid processing is not automatically gravity-independent. |
| **Gemini: rotating 0.05–0.15 g smelting → casting and packaging** | **2–2** | **6–7** | Sustained partial-gravity mould filling, gas removal, solidification, release and hot-product handling lack the required demonstrated basis. Upstream slag separation must also succeed, but is not itself T22. |
| **GPT: native-metal-only production; rotating modules experimentally gated** | **2–2** | **5–6 without melting; 6–7 if rotating casting is required** | Native-metal availability and liberation are upstream conditions. T22 still needs evidence that heterogeneous metal can become an accepted product rather than merely a contained concentrate. |

**Important qualification:** “No-melt” in Claude’s proposal describes the primary metallurgy route. If T22 subsequently melts the powder to make cast stock, it inherits the casting risks; the route label cannot remove them.

## 4. Target, timing and advancement difficulty

- **Internal 0A target:** TRL 4, progressing to TRL 5 for selected critical functions before the 0A completion review.
- **KDP-0B target:** **TRL 6**, with no waiver, for the selected integrated T22 subsystem.
- **Needed by:** **KDP-0B, before commitment to production hardware.** No calendar date for this milestone is supplied.
- **Planning duration:** approximately **6–10 years from funded development start**, assuming access to an appropriate space demonstrator. This is an assessment estimate, not an approved schedule.

**Overall AD²: 6.** Existing industrial processes offer plausible paths, but several competing approaches remain and the acceptable product is not yet defined. AD² could fall to 5 if Phase 1 accepts compacted native-metal stock and testing confirms that this avoids melting and demanding densification. It could rise to 7 if continuous rotating casting proves essential.

The project’s approximate AD² success percentages should not be interpreted as calculated probabilities for T22.

## 5. Development path

**Costs below are broad planning estimates, not quoted programme costs.** They exclude the full mining plant and tug fleet. Flight-payload estimates exclude a dedicated spacecraft unless explicitly stated. Steps overlap; their durations should not simply be added.

| Step | Scale and work | Cost estimate | Duration | Evidence level reached |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Product acceptance and interface definition** | Phase 1-signed specifications; impurity limits; package dimensions; restraint loads; unloading method; sampling rules; abrasion and permissible dust-release criteria. | **$0.3–1.5M** | **0.5–1 yr** | TRL 2; necessary, but paperwork does not advance physical readiness. |
| **Route-specific laboratory proof** | 1–10 kg lots of representative native, reduced and carbonyl-derived Fe–Ni. Compare pellet strength, sintered density, cast quality, contamination and packaging closure. | **$1–5M** | **1–2 yr** | TRL 3. |
| **Integrated terrestrial breadboard** | 100–1,000 kg batches; demonstrate a modular line capable of 75–313 kg/h, with repeated lots, autonomous metrology, rejection and package closure. | **$5–20M** | **1.5–3 yr** | TRL 4, provided measured performance agrees with predictions and the relevant environment is documented. |
| **Reduced-gravity process discrimination** | 1–10 kg experiments for powder feeding, pellet handling, mould filling and release. Parabolic/drop-tower tests establish transient behaviour; rotating ground tests supplement but do not reproduce low absolute gravity. | **$2–10M** | **1–2 yr** | TRL 4; TRL 5 only for functions whose relevant timescales and conditions are actually represented. |
| **Packaging and qualification environmental campaign** | Full-size representative modular packages, up to an assumed 1 t; thermal vacuum, dust, closure faults, restraint loads, abrasion and justified accelerated ageing. Validate autonomous inspection against destructive examination. | **$5–20M** | **1.5–3 yr** | TRL 5 for packaging functions; not automatically for consolidation. |
| **Sustained space process pilot** | 10–100 kg batches; controlled repeated operation in microgravity, or sustained 0.05–0.15 g for the casting branch. Integrate consolidation, acceptance tests, package closure and handling. | **$30–150M incremental payload/integration** | **3–5 yr** | TRL 5 initially; TRL 6 only with representative integration and defensible scaling. |
| **TRL 6 scaling and endurance closure** | Demonstrate at least one representative production module, assumed 0.1–1 t batches, and validate replication to 0.6–2.5 kt/yr. Demonstrate representative package attachment and handling—not necessarily a complete 300 t load. | **$20–80M ground/integration; dedicated flight platform separately** | **2–4 yr**, overlapping pilot | TRL 6 only if the relevant-environment demonstration and validated scaling support the selected architecture. |

A dedicated sustained partial-gravity spacecraft could add approximately **$100–400M and several years**. That estimate has low confidence until the facility is defined.

### Essential modelling and analysis

These support—not replace—the experiments:

- Calibrated powder-flow and contact models for feeding, compaction and abrasion.
- Casting/solidification models validated against the actual rotation, melt depth and residence time.
- Package structural and thermal models validated by load and thermal-vacuum tests.
- Statistical acceptance plans validated against destructive composition/property measurements.
- Throughput and reliability models including rejected lots, maintenance, consumables and autonomous recovery.

A 10 kg orbital experiment is **not automatically TRL 6**. The scaling case must show why its geometry, residence times, interfaces and failure modes represent the production module.

## 6. Risk and fallback

**Integrated failure class: project-ending for 0B**, if no product form can meet signed Phase 1 acceptance and transport requirements. It is not project-ending for funded 0A.

**Individual route failure: architecture-change**, while another route remains viable.

Fallback order:

1. Accept a simpler, explicitly contracted product—such as compacted native-metal stock—if Phase 1 can use it.
2. Use smaller sealed packages and more parallel consolidation modules, accepting increased tare mass, handling and cost.
3. Switch between powder consolidation and casting **only after the replacement route meets its own gate**.
4. If none reaches TRL 6 and the acceptance/economic gates, invoke **“0A only, Earth supply.”**

Increasing centrifugal acceleration is a possible redesign, not a qualified fallback. It requires new validation and may change mass, power and interface requirements.

## 7. Where assessors might disagree

The largest disagreement is **where to draw the technology boundary**.

An assessor rating an ordinary sintered-metal compact or sealed container could reasonably assign high terrestrial maturity. An assessor treating space sample containment as proof of a critical T22 function might assign **TRL 3 to that function**. Neither establishes TRL 3–4 for the complete architecture-specific chain.

The next-largest uncertainty is **Phase 1 acceptance**. A specification allowing porous native-metal stock could substantially simplify T22. A specification requiring dense, homogeneous, low-contamination structural alloy could force melting, additional refining and more demanding qualification. Until signed specifications exist, those alternatives should remain separate.

# T22 Consolidated Rating: Product consolidation, packaging and qualification (Fe-Ni)

**Scope.** All three assessments treat T22 as the step downstream of reduction or smelting. Claude and GPT both say explicitly that silicon refining is out of scope and that smelting and slag separation belong upstream (rq-0-11, rq-0-56). Gemini does not address the re-scoping.

## 1. Summary table

| | Claude Opus 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | GPT-6.1 Sol |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Current TRL** | 2–4 (headline 3) | 2–3 | 2–2 |
| **What the rating applies to** | Each sub-function separately. The headline is the best route, limited by qualification. | Consolidation in general | The integrated, architecture-specific chain |
| **First unmet exit criterion** | TRL 4: no breadboard on representative feed, and no documented relevant environment (Phase 1 spec, tug cargo environment, D-03 allocation) | TRL 4: no kg-scale thermal-vacuum breadboard agreeing with prediction | TRL 3: no results validating the integrated chain on representative feed |
| **AD²** | 5 for the bundle. Native route 5; casting 6–7. | 6 | 6 (range 5–7). No-melt and native routes 5–6; casting 6–7. |
| **Target** | TRL 6 at KDP-0B, no waiver. TRL 4–5 at 0A mid-term (~2029–30, assumed). | TRL 6 at KDP-0B, "needed by 2030" | TRL 6 at KDP-0B, no waiver. Internal 0A goal of TRL 4, moving to 5. |
| **KDP-0B date** | ~2033–2036 (assumed; not dated in the decisions provided) | 2030 (source not given) | Not supplied |
| **Risk class** | Project-ending for 0B, through acceptance and qualification. Consolidation alone is architecture-change. | Architecture-change in §5 and the YAML; §3 calls it "project-ending for Phase 0B" (internally inconsistent) | Project-ending for 0B. Failure of a single route is architecture-change. |
| **Years to target** | 6–10 | 4–7 | 6–10, counted from funded start |
| **Path cost (USD)** | ~$133–382M (steps 1–8) | ~$65–140M | ~$63–287M, plus ~$100–400M for a dedicated partial-g spacecraft if needed (low confidence) |
| **Confidence** | Medium | Medium | Medium |

## 2. Where the assessments agree

- **TRL 2 is met.** The concept and its application are documented. No assessor puts the lower bound below 2.
- **The target is TRL 6 at KDP-0B.** Claude and GPT add that no waiver is allowed.
- **Nothing integrated has been demonstrated.** No system consolidates, packages and qualifies representative asteroid-derived Fe-Ni in vacuum or reduced gravity at any meaningful scale.
- **Space heritage is gram-scale.** The levitators, Metal3D and the sample-return containers are all orders of magnitude below the requirement. The size of the gap is quantified differently (see §4).
- **Casting at 0.05–0.15 g is the hardest route.** All three hold it at TRL 2–3 or lower. Claude and GPT give it AD² 6–7. No assessor in this round rated partial-g casting higher. Claude had anticipated that Gemini might, but Gemini's assessment rates it 2–3.
- **Phase 1 acceptance is the unresolved driver** (Claude and GPT).
  - Claude points out that "dust-tight consolidated form" and "Phase 1-accepted" may conflict if Phase 1 wants powder.
  - GPT points out that "a dust-tight pellet is not necessarily an accepted product."
  - Both make a signed specification the first path step.
- **The ultimate fallback is the D-02 pre-committed "0A only, Earth supply"** (Claude and GPT).
- **Some legacy evidence is rejected** (Claude and GPT). The "Nature Chemistry 2025 magnetic electrolysis" citation is not credited. The rq-0-11 deliberation's assertions are not treated as TRL evidence. Claude also drops the UMG-Si 4N–5N claim as out of scope.

## 3. Where they diverge and why

### 3.1 Current TRL: 2–2 vs 2–3 vs 2–4

**What is in dispute.** Two questions, linked:
- Where the technology boundary is drawn.
- Whether evidence from outside the architecture counts toward TRL 3.

**Each position and its basis.**
- **Claude** gives the no-melt route TRL 3. The basis is terrestrial powder-metallurgy and HBI densification data (E1, E2). Claude withholds TRL 4 because terrestrial feed is unrepresentative: residual S, P and C, and carbonyl residues.
- **Gemini** gives TRL 3. The basis is gram-scale microgravity sintering (German et al.) and powder additive-manufacturing work (D'Angelo 2021). Both citations are marked confident by Gemini, but Claude marks both unsure and GPT declines to credit D'Angelo (see §4).
- **GPT** gives TRL 2. GPT accepts that the individual elements (sintering, containers) are mature, but states that nothing validates the *architecture-specific chain* on representative feed. GPT notes that an assessor rating a single function, such as sample containment, could reasonably give that function TRL 3.

**What would settle it.**
- A panel ruling on the T22 boundary: individual functions or the integrated chain.
- Documented results from representative-feed experiments. These are Claude step 2 and GPT step 2: 1–100 kg of carbonyl, H₂-sponge and native-metal concentrate containing troilite, P, Co and attached silicate.
- For Gemini's TRL 3 basis specifically: verification of what German et al. and D'Angelo et al. actually demonstrated.

### 3.2 AD²: 5 vs 6

**What is in dispute.** Whether the competing consolidation options are an unresolved fork in the path.

**Each position and its basis.**
- **Claude (5).** The options (press, briquette, sinter, nickel vapour deposition, canister) are fallbacks for one another, not a fork. The path is clear provided a no-melt or native route stays open. Claude would move to 6–7 if the programme converges on casting.
- **Gemini and GPT (6).** There are several competing approaches with no down-select, the product definition is open, and the gravity environment is contested. GPT says AD² could drop to 5 if Phase 1 accepts compacted native-metal stock.

**What would settle it.** A signed Phase 1 product specification and a route down-select. Both assessors' positions converge depending on which way those go.

### 3.3 Risk class

**What is in dispute.** Whether lot qualification and acceptance belong inside T22.

**Each position and its basis.**
- **Claude and GPT.** Acceptance has no fallback within the architecture. If no product is accepted, the D-02 demand and economics gates fail. That makes T22 project-ending for 0B.
- **Gemini.** Rates T22 architecture-change, with sealed bladders as the fallback. However, Gemini's own §3 calls packaging and qualification "project-ending for Phase 0B". The conflict is unresolved inside that assessment.
- **Claude's own caveat.** Claude flags the bundling as contestable. If acceptance is moved under the D-02 demand gate, T22 would become architecture-change with a TRL 5 target.

**What would settle it.**
- A panel boundary decision on whether acceptance sits in T22 or the D-02 demand gate.
- Gemini to reconcile its §3 and §5.

### 3.4 Schedule: 4–7 yr and "2030" vs 6–10 yr

**What is in dispute.** How long the path takes and when KDP-0B falls.

**Each position and its basis.**
- **Gemini** gives 4–7 years and a 2030 need date. No source is given for the date, and Claude and GPT both state that KDP-0B is undated in the decisions provided.
- Gemini's path is also shorter: three steps, ending in a 10–100 kg pathfinder.
- **Claude and GPT** include steps Gemini omits: the specification, representative feed, a qualification instrument suite, a packaging campaign and a scaling closure.

**What would settle it.** A programme-dated KDP-0B, and agreement on which path steps are mandatory.

### 3.5 Is a 10–100 kg flight demonstration sufficient for TRL 6?

**What is in dispute.** What flight scale, and what supporting evidence, qualifies for TRL 6.

**Each position and its basis.**
- **Gemini.** A 10–100 kg pathfinder reaches TRL 6.
- **Claude.** Requires a flight of 0.1–1 t of product, at least 6 months of operation, and a Phase 1 witness test. Claude names whether ground thermal-vacuum testing alone could justify TRL 6 for solid-state consolidation as "the main contestable call".
- **GPT.** "A 10 kg orbital experiment is not automatically TRL 6." GPT requires a separate scaling and endurance closure on a representative production module (0.1–1 t batches).

**What would settle it.** A documented scaling argument showing that the demonstrator's geometry, residence times, interfaces and failure modes represent the production module. Also, a panel position on whether solid-state pressing and sintering are gravity-insensitive once the die is filled. Reduced-gravity die-fill and powder-feed tests (all three paths include these) bear directly on that question.

### 3.6 Required rate basis

| Assessor | Rate basis | Resulting rate |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | 100% duty | 70–290 kg/h |
| Claude | 40–60% availability | 120–700 kg/h |
| GPT | 8,000 h/yr of operation | 75–313 kg/h |
| Gemini | Per day | 2–7 t/day |

Only GPT states a tug payload (150–300 t). For package hold time, Claude gives 1.5–5 years plus SEL1 storage; GPT uses 5 years as a conservative assumption; Gemini does not state one.

**Why it matters.** The rate basis sets the scale of the ground breadboard (§5, step 4).

**What would settle it.** A plant availability requirement and a trajectory-specific hold-time requirement.

### 3.7 Fallback content

| Assessor | Fallback order |
|---|---|
| Claude | 1. Loose product in sealed canisters, if Phase 1 wants powder. 2. HBI-style briquetting only. 3. Full vacuum sintering. 4. D-02 fallback. |
| Gemini | Powder or chunks in heavy sealed reusable bladders, accepting a mass penalty. |
| GPT | 1. A simpler contracted product, such as compacted native stock. 2. Smaller packages run in parallel. 3. Switch route, only after the new route passes its own gate. 4. D-02 fallback. |

GPT adds that raising the centrifugal acceleration is a redesign, not a qualified fallback.

The power figures attached to Claude's fallbacks (under 0.3 MJ/kg for briquetting, ~0.55 MJ/kg for sintering, 100–200 kW with losses) are Claude's own estimates. Claude says they are not test results.

### 4.3 Strongest evidence

- **For containment heritage and its failure mode:** OSIRIS-REx and Hayabusa2. These are flight-proven in a real NEA environment and corroborated by two assessors for OSIRIS-REx.
- **For terrestrial consolidation maturity:** HBI and carbonyl powder production (Claude) and the ASM Vol. 7 compilation (GPT). These carry the most weight on process physics, but all assessors agree they say nothing about feed, environment or autonomy.
- **For gravity effects on metal processing:** EML and Metal3D. These are corroborated, but gram-scale and on crewed hosts.
- **The weakest load-bearing items** are German et al. and D'Angelo. They are Gemini's main basis for TRL 3, and both are flagged by other assessors. They should be verified before any rating relies on them.

### 4.4 Absences noted

Claude and GPT both report that none of the following exists:
- Consolidation of representative asteroid Fe-Ni at any scale.
- Bulk powder handling at 0–0.15 g for longer than parabolic-flight durations.
- A Phase 1 product specification.
- Autonomous in-space acceptance for interstitials (O, C, S, N) or for mechanical properties.

Gemini notes that no bulk casting has been demonstrated in space.
